question.worked_solution:
We begin by completing the square for the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
{y}^{2}-11y+30
$$

First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{y}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{11}{2}y+30
$$

Then, we *add* and *then subtract* ${(\frac{11}{2})}^{2},$ writing the constant term $30$ last:

$$
{{y}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{11}{2}y+{(\frac{11}{2})}^{2}}_{⏟}-{(\frac{11}{2})}^{2}+30
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
{(y-\frac{11}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{11}{2})}^{2}+30
$$

Evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
{(y-\frac{11}{2})}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Finally, we substitute this result back into our original expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}-({y}^{2}-11y+30) & =-({(y-\frac{11}{2})}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =-{(y-\frac{11}{2})}^{2}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-{(y-\frac{11}{2})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
